Why does the 4g suck in my area? But, I drive 2 minutes and 4g is solid at max connection? There doesn't seem to be any transition. It's either maxed 4g or stuck on 3g.

There's a couple of things that it could be, but to be frank, the most likely explanation is that there is no explanation. Sometimes cellular towers just have a lot of trouble filling in certain areas, and nobody in the entire company for the entire time I've been working for them has been able to appropriately explain it to me. Over my years in cellular, though, I've accumulated a decent list of excuses given to me by various customer support reps. Here are the most common themes.

If you're using an android, go into networks in your settings and switch your network type from Automatic to LTE/CDMA. When it's set to automatic, it will try to connect to all sorts of towers your phone is denied access from. When that happens, it drains your battery quicker, and makes it harder for your phone to create beamforming with a tower. This can affect your reception.

If you have an older phone, the antenna probably isn't optimized for the service expansion Sprint has been doing this year. If you have an upgrade ready, getting a new phone might help with your reception. I have nothing to gain by telling you this, by the way, the chances of you walking into my store specifically and buying from me specifically so that I get commission off of you are practically negligible. If you're a fan of iPhone, or the Galaxy Note series, I recommend waiting until September, which is when those phones are usually launched.

If you are in any sort of structure with metal roofing or sheeting around/inside the walls, your reception inside of that building will be practically nil.

If you are located in a valley or gulch, the geography around you could be blocking signal. A lot of this depends upon your location vs the tower's.

I shit you not, if you are too close to a tower, you will get shitty reception. It's hard for me to explain without being able to like draw it out, but basically the signal will pass right over your head if you're too close to the tower.

If you're having exceptionally shitty reception one day, try power cycling your device. If that doesn't work, go to your phone's dial pad and dial ##873283# (which translates to ##UPDATE#) and hit send (if it doesn't automatically send after entering the last # sign). This will update your phone's tower list and put local tower info into your phone's RAM, which will allow for smoother transitioning between towers and faster overall reception.

If all else fails, try to get a replacement for your phone. As perfect as we want our phones to be, the fact is that they come off of an assembly line thousands at a time, and there's absolutely no way that every single phone is going to be perfect. There's also absolutely no way that the manufacturer is going to be able to catch all of the defects before they get shipped out. This is just the reality of the situation. All phones are covered under a one year manufacturer's warranty, so if you've had the phone for a year or less and it's in good physical shape (no cracks, no water damage, no chunks missing, etc.), you can probably get a free replacement. If your phone is physically damaged, you will either need to upgrade to a new phone or pay an insurance deductible to have a replacement phone shipped to you through Asurion. (While we are on the subject of defective devices, I want to bring up the fact that Sprint does not make the phones. Samsung, LG, Apple, HTC, Motorola, and other manufacturers are the ones responsible for you ending up with a defective device. There is absolutely no benefit to be had from getting snippy with a Sprint rep because, "You sold me a bad phone!" No, I sold you a brand new phone in a box that had never been opened before, and I had no different expectations about that phone being defective than you did. We are just as pissed as the customer when they are given a defective phone. You think we want you coming back and bitching at us over a defective phone? No, we just sell the shit and pray that Sprint's back end doesn't fuck up your bill.)

If you're having trouble getting good reception at home, you can contact customer care and see about getting a booster installed at your house. I've had some customers tell me this is free, I've had other customers tell me it costs money. I'm not sure one way or the other, to be honest, because contrary to popular belief, store reps for Sprint are only trained on the tip of the iceberg for the whole company. Never once was I told about or trained on these boosters, I had to learn about their existence through my customers.

If none of that helps, you're probably just shit out of luck, my friend. Sprint's reception has actually been improving a lot recently, but I'm not about to tell you we're the best or anything. We are going to have dead spots, and we are going to have spots where reception isn't so good. Hard to secure the funds to improve the towers or build new ones when we have a name for being the least expensive national carrier. Also doesn't help that Sprint has been in the red since the Nextel merger, which was over a decade ago. ¯_(ツ)_/¯
